hypothesis: If Arizona climate fluctuated with a regular period of almost exactly 150 years over the last 500 years, then 100-year-smoothed ring-width chronologies of Arizona ponderosa pine will show a spectral peak at 135-165 years that is significant against a red-noise null, and that peak will recur across independent sites.
pass_criterion: Use all ITRDB Pinus ponderosa chronologies from Arizona that cover at least AD 1450-1950, as separate series. Standardize each one, then apply a 100-year smoothing filter as Douglass did. Estimate the multitaper spectrum over the 500 years ending at the last common year, and over AD 1450-1950 for comparison. The claim passes if both conditions hold. (a) In at least 2/3 of the chronologies, the highest spectral peak in the 80-300 year range lies at 135-165 years and exceeds the 95% confidence level against an AR(1) red-noise Monte Carlo null (1000 surrogates). (b) The band 135-165 years holds at least 25% of the smoothed-series variance in the pooled mean chronology, and the peaks in different chronologies are coherent (squared coherence >= 0.6 at the 150-year band).
fail_criterion: The claim fails if fewer than 1/3 of the chronologies have a significant (95% red-noise) peak at 135-165 years. It also fails if the dominant peak in the pooled mean chronology lies outside 135-165 years. It also fails if the 135-165 year band holds less than 10% of the smoothed variance. Anything between pass and fail counts as inconclusive, and the claim is not supported.
interpretation: 'Century-smoothed annual ring widths' means standardized ring-width indices passed through a 100-year running mean or low-pass filter. 'Regular periodicity of almost precisely 150 years' means a narrow, statistically significant spectral line near 150 years (135-165 years allows for resolution limits), not just a red-noise low-frequency trend. 'Yellow pines' means Pinus ponderosa. 'Arizona climate' is read as the common signal across Arizona sites, mainly moisture (ring width tracks precipitation). Modern reinterpretation: spectral analysis with red-noise testing replaces Douglass's visual periodogram. The 500-year window holds only about 3 cycles, so the test also reports its resolution and power limits. Temperature and moisture are not separated by this test, and the 'probably mainly moisture' clause is not tested.

dataset.name: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (ITRDB)
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI), World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
dataset.why_it_fits: ITRDB holds public ring-width measurements and chronologies (.rwl and .crn files) for many Arizona Pinus ponderosa sites, including long records from the Flagstaff area that cover the last 500 years or more. Fields used: species code (PIPO), state (Arizona), year, and standardized ring-width index, plus sample depth to restrict analysis to well-replicated years. Because many independent sites exist, a regular 150-year cycle can be checked for replication.
